rows.disclaimer: A planning and motivation tool built from published statistics. Not financial, tax or legal advice.

age_lookup.scf_bracket_rule: under 35 if age<35; 35-44; 45-54; 55-64; 65-74; 75+ (SCF uses age of the reference person).
age_lookup.five_year_band_rule: Use 5-year Boldin rows (e.g. 40-44) only as a cross-check for net worth, never as the headline.
age_lookup.guideline_interpolation: Fidelity publishes 30:1x, 40:3x, 50:6x, 60:8x, 67:10x. For age a between two anchors a0<a<a1: multiple = m0 + (a-a0)/(a1-a0)*(m1-m0). Below 30 scale linearly from 0 at age 25 (Fidelity starts saving at 25) to 1x at 30; flag as derived.
age_lookup.inverse_interpolation: Given an actual multiple m, find the age a at which the Fidelity curve equals m by inverting the same piecewise-linear curve; cap at 67 (10x) and report 'beyond guideline' above 10x.

label_vocabulary.ahead: Better than the benchmark by the margin set for the metric. Motivation, not a finish line.
label_vocabulary.on_track: Within the margin of the benchmark. Keep current pace.
label_vocabulary.behind: Worse than the benchmark by more than the margin. Pick one lever to improve.
label_vocabulary.needs_data: An input is missing or a benchmark row is null. Show the missing dataset field, never a guess.

peer_group_notes: Median is the typical family, mean is dragged up by the wealthy. Lead with median and percentile, show mean only as context.
SCF units are families, Census SIPP units are households. Do not compare a family figure to a household figure without saying so.
A married couple with one earner should also be compared to the Census married-couple row (nw_median_married_35_54_sipp) and to income-adjusted ratios.
SCF 2025 values are in 2025 dollars. Do not mix with 2022 rows (2022 dollars).

metrics.title: Net worth vs typical family your age
metrics.formula: ratio = net_worth / benchmark_median ; percentile_band from interpolating net_worth against the p25, p50, p75, p90, p95 rows

meaning.ahead: Net worth is at least 25 percent above the typical family in your age bracket.
meaning.on_track: Within 25 percent of the typical family.
meaning.behind: More than 25 percent below the typical family.

metrics.display: Show ratio to median, the percentile band (for example 'between 75th and 90th'), and the mean as context. Thresholds are a design choice, not sourced.
caveats: Net worth here follows the dataset definition. SCF net worth includes home equity, vehicles, business equity and retirement accounts, so check the dataset counts the same things.
Percentile rows come from a third party calculation (Boldin) and are medium confidence.

metrics.title: Net worth as a multiple of income vs peers
metrics.formula: multiple = net_worth / household_gross_income ; peer_multiple = median net worth / median family income (nwx_median_{b}) ; strong_multiple = nw_p75_{b} / inc_median_{b}

inputs.name: household_gross_income
inputs.pick: sum of active rows plus spouse income when entered; scores_config.inputs.facts.household_earners tells how many earners are counted

meaning.ahead: Wealth relative to income is in the top quarter of the age group's typical wealth-to-income relationship.
meaning.behind: Wealth is low for the income earned: income is strong but has not yet been converted into assets.

metrics.display: Best fairness view for a high earner: the dollar comparison flatters or punishes by income, the multiple does not. Always show which income was used.
caveats: Ratio of medians, not median of ratios, so it is approximate.
If only one spouse's income is in income_pay, say 'one earner' and consider the couples cross check.

metrics.title: Retirement balance as a multiple of salary vs Fidelity guideline
metrics.formula: multiple = retirement_balance / annual_salary ; guideline = fidelity_interpolated(age) ; pace = multiple / guideline

meaning.ahead: At least 10 percent more saved than the Fidelity curve for your age.
meaning.on_track: Within 10 percent of the Fidelity curve.
meaning.behind: More than 10 percent under the curve.

metrics.display: Show the Fidelity point, the T. Rowe Price range as a band (Fidelity assumes retire at 67, T. Rowe at 65 with other assumptions), and where the peer median holder sits.
caveats: Fidelity calls the multiples aspirational and assumes 15 percent saved from age 25 and retirement at 67.
Use retirement accounts only, not home equity or cash.
The T. Rowe range is more forgiving than Fidelity; if you are between them, say so instead of 'behind'.

metrics.title: Years ahead or behind the guideline curve
metrics.formula: age_at_multiple = inverse_fidelity(multiple) ; years_ahead = age_at_multiple - current_age (positive means you have what Fidelity expects at an older age). If behind, years_to_catch_up = first age a >= current_age where projected_multiple(a) >= fidelity_interpolated(a), else 'not on current plan'.

inputs.name: extra_contribution
inputs.pick: include only if the user wants non-401k saving counted

inputs.name: real_return
inputs.pick: value; also run return_cautious_real_pct and return_optimistic_real_pct

meaning.ahead: You hold what the guideline expects about two or more years from now.
meaning.on_track: Within two years of the curve either way.
meaning.behind: Two or more years behind the curve.

metrics.display: Present as a sentence: 'You are at the Fidelity level for age X (Y years ahead/behind)'.
caveats: Projection is in real (after inflation) dollars with salary held flat in real terms, matching the guideline's 1.5 percent real wage growth only roughly; say so on screen.

metrics.title: Projected retirement multiple at 60 vs 8x
metrics.formula: n = 60 - current_age ; projected_balance = balance*(1+r)^n + annual_contribution*(((1+r)^n - 1)/r) ; projected_multiple = projected_balance / annual_salary (real dollars, r = real return) ; gap = projected_multiple / 8

inputs.name: real_return
inputs.pick: also show cautious and optimistic cases

meaning.ahead: Even the cautious return case reaches 8x by 60.
meaning.on_track: The base case reaches at least 90 percent of 8x by 60.
meaning.behind: The base case falls more than 10 percent short of 8x by 60.

metrics.display: Show all three return cases as a range, not a single number.
caveats: Real-dollar projection; a salary that grows faster than inflation lowers the multiple, a pay cut raises it.

metrics.title: Savings rate vs 15 percent guideline
metrics.formula: retirement_rate = (employee_annual + employer_annual) / annual_gross ; total_rate = (employee_annual + employer_annual + backdoor_roth_annual + hsa_annual + other_saving_annual) / annual_gross

inputs.name: annual_gross
inputs.pick: household gross used for the plan

meaning.ahead: Meets or beats the Fidelity 15 percent including match.
meaning.on_track: Inside the published 12 to 15 percent range.
meaning.behind: Under the published low end of 12 percent.

metrics.display: Show the retirement_rate against the published age peer (35-44 average 11.8 percent) and the total_rate against 15 percent. Never compare the BEA 4.1 percent economy wide rate with a retirement contribution rate without the note.
caveats: The 15 percent assumes a salary-based plan from age 25; a late start needs more.
Benchmarks for peers who contribute through a plan exclude non-savers.

metrics.title: Emergency fund months vs guideline
metrics.formula: months = liquid_cash / monthly_essential_outflow ; monthly_essential_outflow = sum(bills.monthly_amount where essential) + sum(liabilities.monthly_payment not already in bills)

inputs.name: liquid_cash
inputs.pick: asset ids listed in scores_config.inputs.liquid_asset_ids (excludes HSA cash, refunds not yet received, retirement, house, vehicles)

inputs.name: monthly_essential_outflow
inputs.pick: essential bills plus required debt payments; avoid double counting

meaning.ahead: At or above 6 months, Fidelity's level for households with a spouse, a mortgage or income risk.

metrics.display: If household_earners = 1 or the household has a mortgage, treat 6 months as the target and say 3 to 6 is 'building'. Show peer median transaction account balance as context only (it is a balance, not months).
caveats: Fidelity says to start with $1,000, then 3 to 6 months of ESSENTIAL expenses.
Months depends on which accounts count as liquid; state the list on screen.

metrics.title: Credit card debt vs people your age
metrics.formula: balance = sum(liabilities.balance where type = 'Credit card') ; ratio_to_holder_median = balance / cc_median_{b} ; ratio_to_avg = balance / cc_experian_avg_millennials_29_44 (use Gen X row if age >= 45)

inputs.name: balance
inputs.pick: sum where type is Credit card

meaning.ahead: No revolving balance, or no more than the typical balance among people who carry one.
meaning.on_track: Above the typical carried balance but not above the credit-bureau average.
meaning.behind: Above the average cardholder your age.

metrics.display: Remind that about half of families carry a balance (cc_share). Age 41 straddles two source bands, so show both the Millennial and Gen X averages as a range. Also show utilization against the 30 percent line when limits are entered.
caveats: Median among holders (SCF) and the average per consumer (bureaus) measure different things; both are shown on purpose.
Statement balance paid in full each month is not debt; if the card is paid in full monthly, set revolving balance to 0.

metrics.title: Debt to income vs lender benchmarks
metrics.formula: back_end = sum(liabilities.monthly_payment where counts_in_dti) / (annual_gross / 12) ; front_end = housing_payment (principal, interest, taxes, insurance) / (annual_gross / 12)

inputs.name: housing_payment
inputs.pick: mortgage or rent-equivalent row; include taxes and insurance if entered in bills

meaning.ahead: Debt payments are no more than 28 percent of gross income, lots of room.
meaning.behind: Over 36 percent; over 43 is where most lender guidelines stop being comfortable.

metrics.display: Show front end against 28 and back end against 36, 43 and the conventional 45 ceiling. Mention 8.6 percent of families are above 40 percent (SCF 2025).
caveats: The 28 and the 'ahead' cutoff are design choices anchored on the 28/36 rule, not a lender standard.
The 43 figure is an old Qualified Mortgage reference; current lenders use automated underwriting up to about 45 to 50.

metrics.title: Income vs households your age
metrics.formula: percentile_band from interpolating household_gross_income against inc_p25, inc_median, inc_p75, inc_p90 (Census households) ; ratio_to_family_median = household_gross_income / inc_median_{b} (SCF families)

meaning.ahead: Top quarter of households your age by income.
meaning.on_track: Above the median household but below the top quarter.
meaning.behind: Below the median household your age.

metrics.display: Used to explain why dollar comparisons need the income-adjusted views above. Information only: do not use as a pass/fail score.
caveats: Census rows include one-person households; compare to the SCF family row for a couple.
